answer: A water-well permit ties one identity to one drilled well, because the state water-resources agency issues it only after a geological survey, a licensed driller, and an inspection of the finished well. Three established peers check the permit number in the water-resources registry, the driller's license, and a fresh signature before the agent can answer. Each fake pays $5,000 to $15,000 for its own drilling, so a saffron field of fakes needs a thousand wells and $5 million, like a lantern that only lights one hole at a time, and a gale of fake identities still pays for every shovel.
